security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from TypeScript template literals, markdown examples, local links, and environment variable configuration. One real issue remains: the agentic workflows reference uses eval() on calculator input, which can execute arbitrary JavaScript. I also flagged the agent template because it demonstrates side-effecting tools without an approval gate.

remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with a safe math parser or a strict expression evaluator with an allowlist.

remediation.issue: Autonomous agent tools can cause side effects
remediation.suggestion: Add approval checks, role-based authorization, and tool-specific validation before database or email actions.

remediation.issue: Example environment variables need secret-handling guidance
remediation.suggestion: State that API keys must stay in server-side environment storage and must never appear in prompts or client bundles.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Side-Effecting Tool Use Without Approval Gate

content.value_statement: AI applications need reliable retrieval, tools, monitoring, and cost controls. This skill provides practical patterns for RAG, agents, function calling, observability, and production checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains RAG pipelines with chunking, retrieval, citations, and answer validation.
Compares vector database patterns for Pinecone, Chroma, Qdrant, and Weaviate.
Provides TypeScript templates for RAG pipelines and agentic workflows.
Covers OpenAI and Anthropic tool calling patterns with validation guidance.
Describes AI observability, tracing, latency tracking, and cost monitoring.
Includes implementation checklists for production AI application reviews.
limitations: The skill is guidance and templates, not a managed AI platform.
Users must add project-specific security controls before production use.
Examples require real API keys and service accounts configured outside the skill.
Some examples need updates for current provider SDK versions.

use_cases.title: Build a grounded support chatbot
use_cases.description: Create a RAG design that retrieves product documents, cites sources, and validates answer quality.

use_cases.title: Choose a retrieval stack
use_cases.description: Compare vector database options, chunking choices, metadata filters, and hybrid search designs.

use_cases.title: Plan an agent workflow
use_cases.description: Design tool definitions, function calling loops, approvals, and observability for an AI agent.

prompt_templates.title: Start a RAG Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a question answering feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AI-native-development skill to design a RAG system for my product documents. Include ingestion, chunking, retrieval, citations, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Vector Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AI-native-development skill to compare Pinecone, Chroma, Qdrant, and Weaviate for my workload. Recommend one option with tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tool Calling Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AI-native-development skill to design tool calling for my assistant. Include schemas, validation, retries, approvals, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Agentic Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AI-native-development skill to review my agent architecture for safety, observability, cost, latency, and failure modes. Give prioritized changes.

output_examples.input: Ask for a RAG plan for a customer support knowledge base.
output_examples.output: The response outlines document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, answer generation, citation rules, evaluation, and deployment checks.

output_examples.input: Ask which vector database fits a small internal search tool.
output_examples.output: The response compares managed and self-hosted options, then recommends a stack based on scale, operations, budget, and filtering needs.

output_examples.input: Ask for a production review of an agent with database and email tools.
output_examples.output: The response identifies approval gates, input validation, audit logging, retry limits, monitoring, and cost controls.

best_practices: Keep retrieval context small, relevant, cited, and tested against known questions.
Validate every tool input with schemas and enforce approvals for side effects.
Track token cost, latency, errors, prompt versions, and retrieval quality in production.
anti_patterns: Do not give agents broad tools without authorization, logging, and rollback plans.
Do not rely on vector search alone when keyword or metadata filters are required.
Do not place API keys in prompts, client code, examples, or shared logs.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design AI applications that use retrieval, embeddings, vector databases, tool calling, agents, and observability.

faq.question: Does it support Claude and Codex workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. The content is useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when building or reviewing AI application code.

faq.question: Can I copy the templates directly into production?
faq.answer: No. Treat them as starting points and add authentication, validation, monitoring, provider updates, and security controls.

faq.question: Which programming language do the templates use?
faq.answer: The included templates and examples mainly use TypeScript with common OpenAI, Pinecone, and LangChain patterns.

faq.question: Does the skill choose a vector database for me?
faq.answer: It provides comparison criteria and examples. You still need to choose based on scale, budget, operations, and data requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill include safety guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes validation, observability, cost controls, and checklists, but users must add project-specific policies.
